title: CO₂: ideal gas against van der Waals
caption: 1 mol of CO₂ at 300 K in 1.0 L. Ideal gas: p = RT/V = 24.9 bar. Van der Waals, with a = 0.364 Pa m⁶ mol⁻² and b = 4.27 × 10⁻⁵ m³ mol⁻¹: p = RT/(V − b) − a/V² = 26.0 − 3.6 = 22.4 bar. The excluded volume b raises p; the attraction term a/V² lowers it, and here the attraction wins.
alt: Graph of pressure against volume for CO2 at 300 K: the ideal hyperbola and the lower van der Waals curve; at 1 litre they read 24.9 and 22.4 bar.
description: The horizontal axis is volume in litres, the vertical axis pressure in bar.
The ideal-gas curve p = 24.9/V passes through 24.9 bar at 1.0 L.
The van der Waals curve lies below it at moderate volumes (attraction), 22.4 bar at 1.0 L.
The two curves agree at large volume, where the molecules are far apart.
